verdict.summary: Building and testing OAuth in a free development workspace is quick, but a public app stays private to your own team until Intercom reviews it, so no customer can connect before approval. Review is a light, single pass (up to seven business days) that needs an end-to-end OAuth video and tight scopes, after which the app goes live as public-unlisted.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Create a development workspace, create an app in the Developer Hub, turn on 'Use OAuth', add an HTTPS redirect URL. Development workspaces get OAuth automatically.

timeToProd.assumes: A public unlisted app that reads and writes conversations, tickets and contacts in customers' workspaces; App Store listing is a separate optional step after approval.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Intercom app review (stated as up to seven business days), plus resubmission time if scopes or the video are rejected.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The seven-business-day figure is Intercom's stated review window. The upper end allows one rejection and resubmission, which is our estimate.

prerequisites.why: Apps are created in the Developer Hub of a workspace; development workspaces come with OAuth enabled.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: We confirmed the developer sign-up page loads; its pricing wasn't stated in the docs we read.

prerequisites.item: HTTPS redirect URLs (test and production can both be registered)
prerequisites.why: Intercom requires HTTPS redirect URLs; the first is the default and others are chosen with redirect_uri.

prerequisites.item: Test credentials or setup instructions for your own service
prerequisites.why: Reviewers need to exercise the full app if it requires an account with you.

prerequisites.item: Privacy policy URL and support email (for an App Store listing)

scopeTiers.tier: Private app on your own workspace (access token)
scopeTiers.impact: No OAuth or review, but it only reaches your own workspace. Useful for prototyping the agent against real data.

examples: Read and list users and companies
scopeTiers.impact: What a support agent needs. Goes through the normal app review; over-broad scopes are the most common reason for initial rejection.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Intercom shows scopes as labels in the Developer Hub rather than machine strings.

scopeTiers.impact: Same review, but each needs a clear reason visible in your video. Article and AI-content scopes matter for agents that use or update the help center and Fin content.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Intercom doesn't document a separate approval track for extended scopes.

scopeTiers.impact: Deleted data can't be recovered. Expect reviewers to question these unless the use case clearly needs them.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Our reading; Intercom doesn't state approval rates.

steps.title: Create a development workspace
steps.detail: Sign up for an Intercom developer workspace.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: The sign-up page returned HTTP 200 on 2026-10-20. We did not sign up.

steps.title: Create separate dev and production apps
steps.detail: In the Developer Hub, create a development app and a production app. After approval the production app is labelled Public and the dev app stays Private.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: The dev/production split and Public/Private labels appeared in a search summary of Intercom's publishing docs but weren't in the page text we read. The Developer Hub URL pattern is our inference; we didn't sign in.

steps.title: Turn on OAuth and add redirect URLs
steps.detail: On the app's Authentication page, enable 'Use OAuth', add HTTPS redirect URLs (the first is the default), and select the minimum scopes.

steps.title: Implement the OAuth flow
steps.detail: Redirect to https://app.intercom.com/oauth?client_id=...&state=... (app.eu.intercom.com or app.au.intercom.com for EU/AU customers). Verify state on callback, then POST code, client_id and client_secret to https://api.intercom.io/auth/eagle/token. Keep any trailing '=' in the code. Store the token per workspace.

steps.title: Handle region-specific API hosts and uninstall
steps.detail: Route API calls to the customer's region and handle deauthorization by deleting stored tokens; the review video has to show uninstall.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Regional API host details weren't on the pages we read; check the API reference.

steps.title: Trim scopes and draft the review submission
steps.detail: Map every selected scope to a feature, write the app description, install instructions and reviewer test-account instructions.

steps.title: Record the end-to-end video
steps.detail: Show OAuth install with the full client_id and state visible in the URL, the app's full functionality, and OAuth uninstall.

steps.title: Submit for review
steps.detail: Submit the app review form in the Developer Hub (description, test access, installation settings).

steps.title: Intercom review
steps.detail: Review can take up to seven business days. Feedback appears under 'Feedback from Intercom'; fix and resubmit if rejected.

steps.title: Go live as public unlisted
steps.detail: Approved apps become public unlisted, installable from your own site. Provide clear install instructions to customers.

steps.title: Optionally list in the App Store
steps.detail: Complete the App Listing (privacy policy, support email, pricing URL if paid) and App Partner Program pages, then choose 'List in App store' and submit the listing review.

Route requests to US, EU or AU hosts per workspace

blockers.symptom: Other workspaces can't install the app
blockers.cause: Until approved, a public app stays private and can only be used by you and your team.
blockers.fix: Submit the app for review and wait for approval.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The exact error shown to an outside installer wasn't documented.

blockers.cause: Selected scopes don't match what the video shows the app doing.
blockers.fix: Remove unused scopes and resubmit with a video that exercises every remaining scope.

blockers.cause: The code value is wrong, often because a trailing '=' was dropped.
blockers.fix: Pass the code exactly as received, URL-decoded once.

blockers.symptom: Google sign-in fails on the Intercom consent screen for EU/AU customers
blockers.cause: The authorize URL host doesn't match the customer's region.
blockers.fix: Use app.eu.intercom.com or app.au.intercom.com for those customers, or let them pick their region before connecting.

blockers.symptom: Users suddenly need to reconnect with no way to refresh
blockers.cause: Intercom has no refresh tokens; once a token is revoked or the app deauthorized it can't be renewed silently.
blockers.fix: Detect 401s, mark the connection broken and prompt the customer to reauthorize.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Stated by Intercom engineering support in a July 2025 community answer, not in the official docs.

blockers.symptom: HTTP 429 bursts even under the per-minute limit
blockers.cause: Limits are enforced in 10-second windows (one sixth of the per-minute limit).
blockers.fix: Smooth request rate and back off using the rate-limit headers.

nuances.text: Access tokens are long-lived and Intercom doesn't issue refresh tokens; tokens stay valid until the user revokes access or the app is deauthorized.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Intercom staff answer in the community forum (July 2025); the official OAuth page doesn't state token lifetime.

nuances.text: Public apps get 10,000 API calls per minute per app, and the workspace has 25,000 per minute; each public app's limit is separate from other public apps, while private apps share the workspace pool.
Customers in EU and AU regions use regional hosts, so store the region with each connection.
Webhook topics depend on scopes, so pick scopes that cover the events your agent subscribes to.
Approved apps start as public unlisted; App Store listing is a separate step and enrolls you in the App Partner Program.
Never ask customers for their own Access Token; use OAuth for any other workspace's data.
